Good point. They make it sound like it's the hash algorithm's fault. The problem was a combination of three things:

  • Hackers got ahold of their password hashes.
  • A weak password was used, which got brute forced.
  • They likely didn't salt their hashes.

If they had a strong password this wouldn't be a problem. Switching to bcrypt helps because it makes it more costly for a potential attacker to do the brute force.

SHA-256 is fine for passwords as long as you have salted, strong passwords and don't give out your password hashes to the hackers. bcrypt doesn't solve these problems, only makes it more difficult for attackers to brute force.
